comments.author: pagetable
comments.text: The scan quality on the log-log duplex models is remarkable. I zoomed into the cursor hairline on the 1947 unit and you can actually see the wear groove where somebody did decades of multiplication in the 2-4 range. That's a usage histogram etched in celluloid.

replies.author: mantissa
replies.text: OP here — that wear pattern is exactly why I started this project. My grandfather was a structural engineer and the 2-4 range groove lines up with the safety factors he used his whole career. I photographed each rule at 4800 dpi under raking light specifically to capture the wear, not just the markings.

replies.author: bitrotting
replies.text: Please put the raw scans somewhere durable, not just the pretty web viewer. Web viewers die; TIFFs survive.

comments.author: circularc
comments.text: Pedantic correction: the article calls the circular one a "pocket slide rule" but circular rules are properly called slide charts or, if the disc rotates, calculating discs. The distinction mattered for patent fights in the era.

replies.author: offbyfun
replies.text: This is the most slide-rule-community sentence I've ever read, and I say that with love.

comments.author: warmstart
comments.text: I built a browser toy that simulates a virtual slide rule with correct parallax if anyone wants to actually learn how to use one: sliderule-trainer.example.com. Reading this collection made me realize my cursor rendering is wrong — the hairline should sit above both scales, not between them.
